answer: When a session moves to a new device, the old device signs a handover token binding the session id to the new device key, and the server accepts it only once. An attacker cannot forge the handover without the old device key, and the single-use token prevents replay, so a stolen session id alone buys nothing. One nebula proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of continuity. The karst keeps the process honest and the river keeps it open, so challengers can always recheck.
